launcher_icon._doc: The launcher icon, generated from this declaration by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-launcher-icons.py (pattern + category colours + glyphs in 1_cicd/src/data/launcher-icons.json). Never edit the generated res files.

name: cloud-myterminal
description: cloud-myterminal — constellation of three minimally-forked upstream developer apps (Acode code editor / Amaze File Manager / Amaze File Utilities) plus a thin original hub APK. The hub switches between the forks and brokers their data (workspaces, recent files, git status, storage analysis, transfers) to Cloud-SuperApp over signature-gated AIDL + ContentProvider IPC. The shared resource is a hub-owned on-device workspace tree (not a server). Forks are declarative: pinned upstream tag + committed patch series, materialized into gitignored tracker clones at build time. Built via Nix devShell (gradle + AGP + Android SDK + node/cordova for the Acode fork).

engine._doc: Documents the default the WebView's transport.js falls back to (window.MYK_ENGINE_URL || this) — NOT wired into the v1 hub build (no build-time substitution yet); the my-konsole engine binary itself owns the real default.

android._doc: Hub-only application coordinates. The forks carry their OWN applicationId / version (declared per fork in build.json::forks) — they are separate APKs.
android._doc_application_id: UNCHANGED by the #561 rebrand (cloud-ide -> cloud-myterminal). An applicationId IS the install identity: #405/#495 measured that changing it makes Android treat the result as a different app, so the fleet updater's install fails with 'Update failed: versionCode N vs installed M' and the owner has to uninstall by hand. The brand is .name (launcher label, fleet listing) and release.* (asset, image); none of those are identity, so the rebrand ships as an ordinary update over the installed hub.
android._doc_abi_filters: Hub is pure-JVM (no native libs) so ABI filtering is irrelevant to it; kept for schema parity with aa_cloud-superapp / ea_cloud-comms. The forks declare their own abi_filters.
android._doc_gradle_module: The Android module is hub/, not the fleet's default app/. Declared so test-app-names-pattern.sh T6 checks this app's launcher label instead of skipping it in silence (#522: an undeclared nested module is how an app drops out of T6).

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps (Cloud-Comms hub+forks, Cloud-Nav, cloud-myterminal, Cloud-SuperApp). The SAME key signs every app so cross-app signature-IPC + the in-app fleet updater never hit a signature mismatch. KEY LOCATION (raw credential + sops passwords live ONLY in the vault repo): Shared/Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/release.jks (OU=Cloud Constellation) + Shared/Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/signing.secrets.yaml. build.sh::_resolve_signing resolves $VAULT_DIR (default ~/git/cloud-vault) + sops-decrypts the passwords, exporting ANDROID_KEYSTORE_FILE/ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD/ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS/ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD which the gradle signingConfig reads. CI does the same via a vault checkout + the SOPS_AGE_KEY secret. THERE IS NO FALLBACK: if the key is unavailable the build FAILS LOUD telling you to use the one shared key — it never generates or substitutes a random/legacy key.
signing._doc_ssh: The ONE declared ssh key every constellation app uses to reach a phone terminal, resolved exactly like the ONE signing key: from the vault, sops-decrypted by build.sh::_resolve_ssh_key, baked to BuildConfig.CLOUD_SSH_KEY_B64, never hardcoded and never generated. The public half is committed in the open at cloud-u-linux/da__my-konsole/termux/authorized_keys, which is what the env provisions — so a phone trusts the key before any app is installed and there is no paste-this-line setup step. NO FALLBACK: a build without the vault fails rather than shipping an app that mints a key the phone has never heard of.

diagnostics._doc: Hub AboutActivity diagnostics → cloud sink + local download (DiagnosticsPush). Baked into BuildConfig.LOG_SINK_URL / LOG_SINK_STREAM by hub/build.gradle. log_sink_url is our OpenObserve (the Loki-equivalent log store) ingest reached via the PUBLIC first-party analytics collector so NO credential is embedded in the public APK. '{stream}' is replaced with log_sink_stream at runtime. EMPTY url = cloud push disabled (Download logs still works); set it to the confirmed collector ingest path to enable Send logs → cloud. Data-driven — never hardcode in Kotlin.

toolchain._doc: Pinned for reproducibility — all derived in flake.nix. Mirrors aa_cloud-superapp / ea_cloud-comms pins so all the Android projects share one toolchain story. Node is added for the Acode (Cordova) fork's JS/plugin build.

ui._doc: Hub UI defaults baked into BuildConfig. overlay_nav_bar_default: the floating cross-app wrapper bar (NavOverlayService) is DISABLED by default — Cloud-SuperApp now owns the system-wide bar. The code stays; Configs has a toggle (persisted in prefs) for users who run cloud-myterminal standalone. terminal_backend_default: which phone env the terminal SSHes into by default ('termux' or 'nix-on-droid'); the Configs 'Terminal backend' switcher overrides this per-device.

modules._doc: Gradle module graph — settings.gradle iterates this (FIRE rule 6: never hardcode the list). Only the hub is an in-tree gradle module; the three forks are SEPARATE gradle/cordova projects living in their materialized tracker clones, built via `./build.sh build-fork <name>`, never included here.

hub.comment: Thin switcher + IPC broker. Original code (no upstream). Declares the signature permission, the unified IdeProvider (reads), the IIdeService AIDL (actions + push callbacks), the launcher switcher UI, and owns the shared workspace root (data/ide-endpoints.json::workspace.root_path). HUB-SHARING: the broker + updater are structurally identical to cloud-comms-hub — once both exist, extract them into a shared gradle module (see forks/../README) rather than maintaining two copies. cloud-comms scaffolded first, so cloud-myterminal consumes the extracted core; until that extraction lands, this hub mirrors the comms hub deliberately.

libs:web-core._doc: #1371 THE embedded web view: CloudWeb.create(ctx, WebProfile.X), profiles, GPU probe, render-process recovery, shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:core._doc: #743 fleet mesh membership. core DEFINES and REQUESTS CONSTELLATION_DATA and carries libs:devtools by `api` (FleetTokenProvider, FleetMemberReceiver, the MESH_MEMBER package query), so linking it is what makes this app a mesh member every other app can see and reach. Shared BY REFERENCE, like every app's core.

libs:ui-kit._doc: 2026-10-16 owner decision: all apps must be Compose. Shared BY REFERENCE: the fleet's Compose kit (CloudKitTheme + KitPalette) every hub screen paints with.

libs:devtools._doc: Not linked by the app module: libs:core's `api project(':libs:devtools')` resolves against THIS settings, so the include must exist or core fails configuration.

libs:crash._doc: #1122 libs:core `api`s this module (the default crash handler, the local crash sink and the generic crash screen); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:fleetconfig-model._doc: #873 libs:core `api`s this module (the setup provider every app serves, describe / export / apply / status); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:ui-nav-bars._doc: #1352 Configs ▸ General and ▸ About (fleetconfigs): FleetConfigsActivity, started from this app's own menu. Shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:bottomnav._doc: libs:ui-nav-bars' `api` dependency; listed so settings.gradle resolves the path.

libs:ui-icons._doc: libs:bottomnav's dependency; listed so settings.gradle resolves the path.

libs:theme-background._doc: libs:ui-nav-bars' `api` dependency (the page background); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path.

libs:perms._doc: #1360/#1352 libs:ui-nav-bars' `api` dependency: Configs ▸ General ▸ Perms is libs:perms' AppPermsSection, first run asks every never-asked grant.

wake_lock._doc: #787 this terminal's sessions are the SSH shells SshBackend holds open (there is no terminal service here), so TerminalWakeLock takes a partial wake lock while at least one is open and drops it when the last one closes; CloudWakeLock (the same class cld.termux and cld.termux.nix run) decides, and test/test-wake-lock.sh runs it. ON by default; Configs > Wake lock turns it off and the choice persists. No Wi-Fi lock: this app never had one and its shells dial a terminal on the same phone. Read by hub/build.gradle into BuildConfig; the build fails if default_on is not a boolean. State: GET /api/terminal/wakelock (also /api/terminal).

release._doc: Per-APK distribution for the HUB — SAME data-driven pattern as aa_cloud-superapp / ea_cloud-comms build.json::release. build.sh oras-push + gh-release read this block; the GHA workflow (1_cicd/src/cicd/ship-cloud-myterminal.yml) only invokes those engine commands, no hardcoded registry/tag strings. The three forks publish their own OCI artifacts under their own build systems. {sha} → git short sha, {version_name} → android.version_name.

abis._doc: ABI build axis. The hub is pure-JVM (ABI-agnostic); the ONLY native-bearing bundled app is the patched Amaze fork (Rust :file_operations). `build.sh build [abi]` / `build-fork <k> [abi]` / `bundle-forks [abi]` select one. `default:true` is what bare `build` / the CI artifact use; non-default abis get a -<abi> artifact suffix. rust_target = the rust-android-gradle cargo target key (passed as -PcloudIdeRustTargets).

artifact._doc: Path under dist/ to publish. `debug` is the daily-driver build (no ProGuard, real stacktraces, debug keystore) — THE hub app, not a side-by-side variant. asset_name matches `debug` so the engine skips a redundant copy.

ghcr._doc: ORAS push as an OCI artifact (APK is a blob, not a container). One :latest tag plus per-commit sha + per-version tags.

gh_release._doc: GitHub Release attachment. rolling_tag is canonical: one release (default `latest`) the ship workflow overwrites on every main push, so /releases/latest/download/Cloud-MyTerminal.apk is a stable URL. tag_pattern stays for immutable per-tag releases under a tag push (rolling release publishes alongside).

phone_install._doc: Targets for build.sh phone-install — pulls the hub APK from GHCR via curl+OCI HTTP API (no oras dep; works on aarch64 Termux without a Nix shell) and copies it where an Android file manager can see it. Override per-env via PHONE_TARGET.

auto_update._doc: In-app updater config — read at gradle eval time into BuildConfig, then used by the hub's com.diegonmarcos.ide.update package at runtime (same OCI HTTP flow as build.sh oras-pull). Same registry/namespace/image as release.ghcr. The hub self-updates from cloud-myterminal:<tag>; the forks update via the same mechanism once they publish their own images. Mirrors aa_cloud-superapp/build.json::release.auto_update.
auto_update._doc_interval: WorkManager periodic minimum is 15 min. 6h matches typical update cadence + spares battery / data.
auto_update._doc_install: Declared default for the runtime Auto-update toggle (Configs/About → Permissions). 'silent' → USER_ACTION_NOT_REQUIRED (no install prompt) once 'Install unknown apps' is granted; falls back to a prompt without it. 'prompt' → always USER_ACTION_REQUIRED.
auto_update._doc_max_installs_per_pass: Most install sessions ONE unattended background pass may open. A background pass cannot show the system install dialog (Android 10+ blocks background activity starts), so each install it starts leaves a tap-to-install notification holding a PackageInstaller session until the user answers it. Unbounded, one pass over the 40-entry fleet opens 40 and the installer hits Android's 50-session cap - 'Too many active sessions for UID'. The remainder is picked up by the next pass. User-initiated 'Update all' is NOT capped: it runs in the foreground where the dialog appears and sessions resolve at once.

analytics._doc: Consumed by :libs:analytics, which reads THIS file (rootDir) at build time and bakes the values into BuildConfig. Both backends are single-site today, so every app reports into the same site and is told apart by .app — give each app its own site_id once per-app sites exist in Umami/Matomo.

web._doc: #876 Cloud My Terminal as a Kotlin/Wasm page (web/ is its own gradle root; the shared libs' pure-Compose sources arrive through the ab_cloud-libs-shared/web composite). Rendered into 1_cicd/src/cicd/ship-cloud-myterminal-wasm.yml by the workflow generator: `./gradlew wasmJsBrowserDistribution` in `dir`, tested by test/test-myterminal-web.sh, `build/dist/wasmJs/productionExecutable` zipped to `artifact` and attached to the rolling release as `gh_asset`. A mocked page: this app declares no bottom-nav island, so the page is one dense list of mock data. The APK's own ship ignores this directory.

tests._doc: What CI runs to prove this app works. Read by 1_cicd/dist/scripts/cloud-android-test-engine.sh, which ship-cloud-myterminal.yml invokes before it builds. Until #675 this block was absent, so the shell phase printed COVERAGE-GAP and exited 0: the only question this app's pipeline asked was whether Gradle exited 0, and Gradle cannot see that the setup instructions named a port the SSH client never dialled, or that the backend switcher enumerated its two options in Kotlin.

shell._doc_requires: A tester that shells out to a tool which is not installed does not fail — it returns a verdict from the tool's ABSENCE, and for a ban-shaped assertion (`no upstream package id appears here`) that absence reads as a PASS. Naming the tools makes a missing one fatal at the engine's preflight.

links._doc: Where a URL tapped in the terminal opens. Long-press on a link (or on an entry of the pane menu's URL list) opens it in browser_package when that app is installed, else in the phone's default browser; a tap copies it. Baked as BuildConfig.LINK_BROWSER_PACKAGE (LinkOpener.kt); the manifest's <queries> names the same package so the lookup sees it.

configs_pages._doc: Configs > General and Configs > About (libs:ui-nav-bars fleetconfigs, rule 1_cicd/src/data/configs-pages.json, #1352 v2). general.sections: the anchors of the one General page, in order (perms, battery, storage, notifications, ui, language are required; app opens this app's own Configs; update is added after perms by default). about: the hand-written part of the extensive About: tagline, description, features, screens, guide, privacy, backends (ids of ac_cloud-account/build.json::fleet_endpoints, resolved to mesh URLs at build time), related fleet apps, credits for a fork. Permissions, data stores, crash/analytics libs, name, icon, version, build sha and date, repo, licence, origin, crash sink, debug API and changelog are derived, never typed here.

about.tagline: Editor, file manager and tools, joined by one hub
about.description: Cloud MyTerminal is a developer constellation: a code editor, a file manager and file utilities (minimal forks of Acode and Amaze) switched and connected by one thin hub app. The hub shares workspaces, recent files, git status and storage analysis between them over Android IPC. It exists so three strong upstream tools act as one environment without merging their code.
features: Shared workspaces, recent files and git status
One workspace root shared by every tool
guide: Open the hub and pick a tool.
Set the workspace root once; every tool uses it.
Install the tools from Cloud Store when the hub asks.
about.privacy: No ads and no third-party trackers. A crash report is saved on the phone and sent only to the phone's own C3 WebServer over loopback; nothing leaves the device unless you share it. Usage analytics are opt-in and off by default; when allowed, events go only to the owner's self-hosted Umami and Matomo. It calls no fleet service: its data stays on the phone.
about.credits: Upstream: Acode (MIT) by Ajit Kumar, Amaze File Manager and Amaze File Utilities (GPL-3.0) by the Team Amaze. The hub is the fleet's own code.

perms._doc: #1360 every grant this app needs, by libs:perms catalogue id (needs), and the fleet apps that do work for it with the grants THEY must hold (helpers). The ONE declaration: generated into assets/app-perms.json (cloud-android-perms-guard.py --write), drawn by Configs > General > Perms (libs:perms AppPermsSection) with live state, Grant / Open and Grant all, asked at first run (first_run), and reported as 'Missing permission X - Grant' when an operation fails (PermsGate). perms-guard fails when code uses a gated API or another app's engine that is not declared here, or when the manifest and this list disagree.
